Objectives: Dragons, Grubs, Herald and Baron

Neutral objectives win games. Learn what each one gives you, when it spawns, and how to set up so your team gets it.

The objectives at a glance

Epic monsters give your whole team a reward. Here's what's on Summoner's Rift in patch 26.22:

ObjectiveSpawnsWhat it gives
Dragons5:00, then 5:00 after each killA permanent stacking buff; 4 drakes = Dragon Soul
Void Grubs8:00 (3 grubs, one time only, gone at 14:45)Extra damage to towers
Rift Herald15:00 (leaves at 19:45)The Eye of the Herald: a charge that wrecks a tower
Baron Nashor20:00, then 6:00 after each killHand of Baron: stronger champions and minions for 3 minutes
Elder Dragon6:00 after a team gets SoulBurn and execute low-health enemies

If you played in 2025, note that Atakhan was removed at the start of 2026, and Baron is back at 20:00. Use our objective timer tool to track everything during a game.

Dragons and Dragon Soul

Dragons spawn in the bottom river. There are six types: Infernal (damage), Mountain (defense), Ocean (healing), Cloud (move speed), Hextech (haste and attack speed) and Chemtech (tenacity and healing when low). Each drake your team kills gives a small permanent buff of that type.

After the second drake, the map transforms into an elemental map that matches the third drake's type, and every drake after that is that same type. The first team to kill 4 drakes gets the Dragon Soul, a strong permanent bonus. After that, the Elder Dragon takes the dragon pit.

Drakes also give gold to the killer, and they get tougher for a team that already has many: drakes take less damage from the team holding stacks. That makes it easier for the team that's behind on dragons to catch up.

Pro tipA team with 3 drakes is one fight away from Soul. If the enemy has 3, treat the next dragon like a must-win fight, and set up vision 60 seconds before it spawns.

Void Grubs and Rift Herald

The top side river pit holds two objectives before Baron arrives:

  • Void Grubs (8:00): three small monsters that only spawn once and leave at 14:45. Each grub gives your team a stack of Touch of the Void, which makes attacks on towers burn. With all 3, your team summons small Voidmites that help push towers. Grubs are great for teams with strong side laners who want to take towers early.
  • Rift Herald (15:00): when killed, it drops the Eye of the Herald. The holder summons the Herald, and a player can ride her and charge into a tower for huge damage. She leaves at 19:45, just before Baron takes the pit at 20:00.

Since turret plates are permanent now, using grubs or the Herald to break a tower's plates gives gold that never goes away.

Baron Nashor

Baron spawns at 20:00 in the top pit. Killing him gives your whole team Hand of Baron for 3 minutes (lost if you die): bonus attack damage and ability power, faster recalls, and an aura that makes nearby minions much stronger. Baron waves can take towers and even inhibitors on their own.

Baron is very strong but risky. He takes time to kill, and the enemy can attack you from behind or steal him with Smite. The safest time to take Baron is right after your team wins a fight and some enemies are dead.

Common mistakeStarting Baron when the enemy team is all alive and nearby. If they collapse on you while Baron is hitting your tank, you'll lose the fight and maybe the game.

How to set up an objective

Objectives are won before they spawn. Use this checklist about 60-90 seconds before an objective appears:

  1. Push the lanes nearest to it. Mid and bot should push for dragon, mid and top for grubs, Herald and Baron. A pushed lane means the enemy laners have to stay and clear, or lose minions.
  2. Recall and buy. Come back with full health and your new items. See Recall Timing and Tempo.
  3. Take vision. Place wards around the pit, sweep enemy wards with Oracle Lens, and put a Control Ward in the river brush. Wards placed on Faelights get extra vision range.
  4. Group up before it spawns. Arrive together. A team that shows up one at a time loses the fight.
  5. Decide: fight or trade. If the enemy team is stronger, you can trade: take a tower or grubs on the other side of the map instead.

Priority: who controls the objective

Lane priority means your laners have pushed their waves and can move first. If your mid and bot have priority, your team gets to dragon first and can fight on your terms. If the enemy has priority, contesting is risky.

Good teams talk about this: "Our bot is pushed, let's go dragon" or "We can't contest, take grubs instead." Use pings to tell your team (see Teamwork, Pings and Role Quests). Not every objective is worth fighting for. Giving one up to take something else is often the smart play.

Key takeaways

  • Dragons spawn at 5:00. Four drakes give Soul, and then the Elder Dragon appears.
  • Void Grubs (8:00) and Rift Herald (15:00) help take towers, which give permanent plate gold.
  • Baron spawns at 20:00 and makes your minions and team much stronger. Atakhan was removed.
  • Set up 60-90 seconds early: push lanes, recall, take vision, group.
  • If you can't contest, trade for something on the other side of the map.
